app.subtitle: Remote control for MeshCore repeaters
app.notBuilt: This part is not built yet.
home.title: Being built
home.body: This is where you will control your repeaters with your own key. The page is not ready yet.
notfound.title: No such page
notfound.body: This address leads nowhere. Go to the start page.
key.noneLabel: No key in this browser. Create or import one.
key.lockedLabel: The key is locked. Unlock it.
key.unlockedLabel: Key {key} is unlocked. Show key and backup.
display.title: Display on this device
display.phosphorHint: Green or amber on black, in a fixed-width font. Always dark.
update.ready: A new version of mccontrol is available.
update.failed: Could not keep a copy for offline use: {reason}
key.gate.backup_required: Save a backup of your key before you set up a node with it. The browser can lose the key; the backup cannot.
key.gate.confirm_saved: Do you have this key saved somewhere other than this browser?
key.passphrase.hint: At least {min} characters. You need it to unlock the key and to open the backup.
key.fingerprint.enable: Also unlock with fingerprint or face
key.fingerprint.disable: Stop unlocking with fingerprint or face
key.persist.granted: The browser keeps the key's storage.
key.persist.denied: The browser may delete the key's storage. Keep the backup; on an iPhone, add the page to the Home Screen.
dash.allWell: Nothing needs attention: every node with known data was heard on MQTT in the last {hours} hours, no battery is under {volts} V, no last command was refused, and no firmware is behind.
dash.att.notHeard: not heard on MQTT for {hours} h
dash.att.forged: bad signature on the answer to {command}: forged or altered
dash.nothingSince: No results since your last visit,
dash.nothingYet: Nothing sent from this browser yet.
dash.quiet: Not heard on MQTT for {hours} h
dash.empty: No nodes yet. Put your key on a repeater, then find it in its region.
dash.toDiscover: Find nodes that already have your key
node.noKey: There is no key in this browser yet.
node.noWholeKey: Only the first 8 characters of this node's key are known, so commands go unencrypted (v1). Find it again with discovery to learn the whole key.
node.noFacts: Nothing read yet. Send ver, get name or get autoreply.
node.noHistory: Nothing sent to this node from this browser.
node.nameHint: Your name for it here. The name the mesh sees is changed with set name.
node.regionHint: The IATA code its observers use, e.g. JKG. Commands go to that region's topics.
node.forgetBody: It leaves the list and its groups. The node keeps your key and still obeys it; its history stays.
nodes.caption: Your {n} nodes
nodes.empty: No nodes yet. Find them below, or add one by its key.
nodes.refreshFleet: Battery and last heard from Beacon
nodes.discoverTitle: Find the nodes in a region that have your key
nodes.discoverExplain: One signed read (get autoreply) to every node in the region. Only nodes that hold your key answer. It costs each node one command slot and nothing on the air.
nodes.discoverNone: No node in {region} answered. A node answers only when it holds your key and is connected to the broker.
nodes.addByKey: Add a node by its public key
nodes.keyHint: 64 hex characters (or the first 8). The whole key lets commands go encrypted.
nodes.name: Name
send.title: Send
send.lede: A command to one node, several, a group, or every node in a region. It is checked before it is signed.
send.regionExplain: One signed broadcast that every node in the region holding your key runs. Commands that transmit are refused for a broadcast, and so are letters outside plain ASCII.
send.commandHint: Start typing for the list of commands, e.g. ver, get autoreply, region.
send.lacks: This node's image ({version}) has no {feature} feature: it will answer not-allowed.
send.notAdmitted: This node runs {version}, which does not admit this command; it needs {needs}. It will answer not-allowed.
send.someRefuse: {n} will answer not-allowed by their firmware: {names}.
send.v2: Goes encrypted (v2): the node's firmware opens it and its whole key is known.
send.v1: Goes signed but readable (v1): older firmware, or only part of the key is known.
send.perNode: One signed command to each of the {n} nodes in turn, on its own topic.
send.broadcastNote: One broadcast to {region}; {n} of your nodes are expected to answer.
send.confirmRegionBody: Every node in {region} that holds your key runs it at once. You have {n} nodes there; others with your key would run it too.
send.silenceNote: No answer means none arrived in time, not that the node did not run it.
send.locked: The key is locked. Unlock it to sign.
send.res.silentHelp: Nothing came back in time. The node may be off the broker, or answered late.
send.res.forgedHelp: The line on this node's result topic was not signed by its key: forged or altered. The reply was ignored.
send.res.noHelp: The node refused it; see Help for this code.
send.res.finding: This firmware should admit it: the table or the version is wrong.
send.why.broadcastTransmit: a command that transmits may not go to every node at once; the firmware refuses it
send.why.broadcastAscii: a broadcast is plain ASCII: nodes before lou-17 refuse letters such as åäö; send it to each node instead
send.why.oldAscii: {name} runs {version}, which takes plain ASCII only; letters such as åäö need lou-17
send.why.broker: the broker could not be reached: {detail}
send.why.badRegion: a region is its IATA code, 2 to 8 letters or digits
send.why.otaRefused: this node cannot be updated over the control plane: {detail}
history.caption: Commands sent and what came back, newest first
history.keepExplain: The history lives only in this browser. Export it to keep a copy or move it; an import adds what is not already here.
history.importHint: Events already here are skipped; events of another key are left out.
history.imported: Imported {added}; {skipped} already here or unreadable; {foreign} of another key.
groups.none: No groups yet. A group lets you send to several nodes in one go, each on its own topic.
groups.name: Name
groups.sendExplain: One signed command to each of the {n} members in turn. A member that cannot take it is reported and the rest still get it.
groups.deleteBody: Only the group goes; its nodes stay.
sets.title: Command sets
sets.lede: A named list of up to six commands, sent in order and stopped at the first refusal or silence.
sets.pickTarget: Choose a node or a group
sets.argHint: Put in every step where {arg} stands.
sets.name: Name
sets.nameHint: One word. A set with the same name is replaced.
sets.stepsHint: At most {n}. {arg} is asked for when the set runs.
update.title: Firmware
update.unknown: The version is not known yet. Send ver to read it.
update.byHand: {latest} is out. This node cannot take an update over the control plane, so flash it by hand.
update.confirmBody: From {from} to {to}. The node downloads the image, restarts, and is off the air and off the control plane for a few minutes. If the new image fails, it goes back to the old one.
update.stage.restarting: The node took the update and is restarting.
update.stage.checking: Asking its version, {secs} s after the start
update.stage.timeout: The node has not reported the new version yet; it still says {version}. Check again later with ver.
update.stage.cancelled: Stopped waiting; the node may still be updating.
